name: Rivaroxaban
summary: An oral direct factor Xa inhibitor with predictable, once-daily anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism, without routine monitoring.
mechanism: Selectively and reversibly inhibits free and clot-bound factor Xa, reducing thrombin generation and fibrin clot formation.
pharmacodynamics: Dose-dependent inhibition of factor Xa activity and prolongation of prothrombin time.

pharmacokinetics.elimination: Renal (~66%, about half unchanged) and fecal

dosing.adult: Nonvalvular AF: 20 mg once daily with food (15 mg if CrCl 15–50 mL/min); VTE treatment: 15 mg twice daily ×21 days, then 20 mg once daily
dosing.renalAdjustment: Avoid if CrCl <15 mL/min; avoid with strong dual CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors; 15 mg daily for AF if CrCl 15–50 mL/min

safety.pregnancy: Avoid — no adequate human data; bleeding risk
contraindications: Concurrent strong dual CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors (azole antifungals, HIV protease inhibitors)
warnings: Major bleeding (intracranial, GI); reversal agent andexanet alfa
monitoring: Renal function at least annually (more often if impaired)
safety.overdose: Activated charcoal if recent; andexanet alfa for life-threatening bleeding

indications: Stroke prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
Treatment of DVT/PE and prevention of recurrence
VTE prophylaxis after hip or knee replacement
VTE prophylaxis in acutely ill medical patients
clinicalPearls: Rapid onset — missed doses are clinically significant, unlike warfarin.
15/20 mg doses must be taken with food for adequate absorption; 10 mg may be taken fasting.
good: Patients needing predictable oral anticoagulation without INR monitoring.
bad: Patients with severe renal impairment, active bleeding, or poor adherence.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
